summary: Test isolation fix for the QA agent's reliability test suites. Previously, running the session-timeout test suite could silently erase the real session history file in the development workspace (the Sessions list in the UI went empty because of it). Both affected suites now run entirely inside their own temporary data folders and provably never touch the real one.
what_was_done: The session-timeout test suite now creates its own temporary workspace folder before doing anything, so any data the test writes lands only in that folder, and the folder is deleted afterwards

A guard at the end of the suite proves two things every run: the real session history file is byte-for-byte unchanged, and the test actually used its own temporary store (not someone else's directory)

The resource-lifecycle test's 'Session count is bounded' check (RL-2) was failing because it read the real workspace's session file, which is legitimately empty after the earlier wipe — it now creates 80 test sessions in its own temporary store, prunes them, and verifies the store keeps at most 50. The check now genuinely passes, and it got stricter, not weaker
No test was deleted or weakened; no product code was changed
what_was_tested: Session-timeout suite: 12/12 pass including the new untouched-real-store guard
Resource-lifecycle suite: 19/19 pass with RL-2 genuinely green (80 seeded sessions pruned to exactly 50)
Full 11-suite regression battery: 130 tests, 129 pass, 0 fail, 6 expected skips (live-server-gated governor tests)
Real session history file verified byte-identical before/after each individual suite AND after the whole battery (three independent checksum comparisons)
Temporary test stores were created, used, and removed — no leftovers
